evidence.supports: Official Business Council meeting agenda listing the item 'Data Center Ban - Resolution #26-F-112 - Phil Johnson' for the May 26, 2026 meeting.
evidence.quote: Data Center Ban - Resolution #26-F-112 - Phil Johnson

evidence.supports: Reports the resolution was adopted, describing it as the first tribal ban on data centers in the region, and quotes its text.
evidence.quote: In May, the Fallon Paiute Shoshone Tribe became the first in the region to ban the centers on their lands. The resolution brought by tribal council secretary Philip Johnson began with the quote, 'Only when the last tree has been cut down, the last fish caught, and the last river poisoned will we realize that money cannot be eaten.'

decisions.notes: REMOVE: this is a permanent ban, not a temporary pause/moratorium. The Fallon Business Council agenda item is titled 'Data Center Ban - Resolution #26-F-112' (not 'moratorium'), and the only substantive source (KUNR, 2026-09-02) states plainly 'the Fallon Paiute Shoshone Tribe became the first in the region to ban the centers on their lands.' The row's own duration field concedes 'Permanent; no stated end date or review/sunset provision found.' A moratorium tracker should not carry an indefinite ban as an 'active' temporary pause; criterion (a) fails.

evidence.supports: Full signed resolution text: definition of data center (including cryptocurrency mining equipment), scope of the moratorium, 12-month duration, exceptions, and the June 23, 2026 unanimous adoption vote.
evidence.quote: PASSED and ADOPTED by the City Council of the City of Wells on June 23, 2026... AYES: Mayor Gary Pollock, Vice-Mayor Jonathan Goolsby, Councilman Chris Micheli, Councilwoman CR Beth Savedra. NAYES: NONE. ABSENT: Councilman Richard Peltier.

evidence.supports: Confirms unanimous Council approval of Resolution 26-06 and describes the moratorium's purpose and scope.
evidence.quote: The Wells Board of Council has voted unanimously to approve Resolution 26-06, establishing a temporary moratorium on data centers within the City of Wells.

evidence.supports: Statewide roundup independently corroborates Wells' late-June 2026 moratorium.
evidence.quote: Wells, a small city in rural northeast Nevada, passed a moratorium on data center approvals in late June pending recommendations from city staff.

decisions.notes: Verified against the full signed resolution text (Resolution No. 26-06), which confirms the June 23, 2026 unanimous adoption, 12-month term, and data-center/crypto-mining scope. Two independent news accounts corroborate. Genuinely a temporary pause, distinct instrument, no duplicate row for Wells found.

evidence.supports: Signed, adopted text of the moratorium resolution, including its findings, scope, and July 22, 2026 adoption date.
evidence.quote: PASSED AND ADOPTED by the Board of County Commissioners of White Pine County, Nevada, at a duly noticed public meeting held on the 22nd day of July 2026

evidence.supports: Draft resolution text (180-day duration, renewal, exceptions) and staff justification/background presented ahead of the July 22, 2026 vote.
evidence.quote: Section 4. Duration. The Moratorium shall be in effect for a period of one hundred eighty (180) calendar days from the effective date of this Resolution...

evidence.supports: Confirms adoption of Resolution 2026-18 at the July 22, 2026 meeting and the 180-day term.
evidence.quote: During their July 22 regular meeting, the White Pine County Board of Commissioners approved Resolution 2026-18, imposing a temporary 180-day moratorium on accepting, processing or approving land-use applications for data center development.

decisions.notes: Verified against the signed Resolution No. 2026-18 and the staff report draft, both confirming the July 22, 2026 adoption and 180-day term with one renewal option. News account corroborates. No duplicate row found.

evidence.supports: Reports the August 21, 2026 Tribal Council vote banning data centers on Pyramid Lake Paiute homelands.
evidence.quote: Earlier this summer, tribal members proposed a permanent moratorium on the centers within the reservation to the Tribal Council. And on August 21, the data center ban passed, Harry said.

evidence.supports: Independent second source corroborating the August 21, 2026 permanent moratorium vote.
evidence.quote: On August 21, the Tribal Council passed a permanent moratorium on data centers on Pyramid Lake Paiute homelands.

decisions.notes: REMOVE: this is a permanent ban, not a temporary pause/moratorium. Both cited sources (KUNR 2026-09-02 and Wyoming Public Media/KUNC 2026-09-14) describe it as a 'permanent moratorium'/'data center ban' with no sunset; the row's own duration field says 'Permanent; no stated end date found.' No instrument number or primary tribal-council resolution text was located (only secondary news coverage). Fails criterion (a) for the same reason as the Fallon Paiute-Shoshone Tribe row -- an indefinite ban is not a temporary pause and should not be carried as 'active' in this tracker.
